title: GTA VI HDR Setup: Calibrating a TV for Neon and Night Scenes
summary: Preserve shadow detail and comfortable brightness on supported HDR televisions.
intro: Leonida's bright outdoor scenes and nighttime lighting invite display adjustments, but a vivid preset is not the same thing as a well-calibrated picture. Preserve shadow detail and comfortable brightness on supported HDR televisions. This original Digital Racer checklist concentrates on practical choices people can verify directly. Features not yet demonstrated in a final release should be treated as unknown, even when a pre-release video appears convincing.

sections.heading: Start in Game Mode
paragraphs: Select an accurate low-latency picture preset before changing individual HDR sliders. Many televisions alter processing when Game Mode is enabled. Compare from the same seating position and lighting conditions, not two differently edited online screenshots.

sections.heading: Check platform HDR output
paragraphs: Use the console's normal HDR calibration pages and follow their on-screen examples. Peak brightness varies by television, so another player's exact numeric values may crush details on yours. Confirm the TV recognizes an HDR signal.

sections.heading: Avoid excessive dynamic contrast
paragraphs: Dynamic contrast and strong sharpening may produce dramatic lights while hiding small objects in shadow. Disable heavy enhancements temporarily and compare a dark corridor and bright street. Preserve readability instead of maximizing a single spectacular screenshot.

sections.heading: Match black levels correctly
paragraphs: If shadowed areas turn solid black or gray, confirm console output and the TV input's expected video range. Incorrect matching can resemble artistic lighting. Use any in-game brightness setting only after the baseline signal is behaving properly.

sections.heading: Keep motion settings separate
paragraphs: Motion interpolation and HDR affect different parts of the experience. A television that creates interpolated images may add latency without raising the game's rendered frame rate. Evaluate steering and camera movement independently from overall brightness.

sections.heading: Calibrate for normal play
paragraphs: Check a daylight scene, a night scene and an interior before committing to settings. A combination that only improves one promotional image can make ordinary play worse. Consider eye comfort and room lighting as well as contrast.

sections.heading: A reliable final check
paragraphs: Use the current official game and platform controls instead of relying on leaked menus or unrelated downloadable tools. Before changing anything, note the original state and what improvement you expect. Test one adjustment in a comparable situation, then verify that it genuinely improves usability, storage, stability or safety. If the outcome is uncertain, keep the supported default. A launch guide is useful when its advice remains accurate after small patches, region differences and individual hardware variation.

Compare your current setup with the conditions above and identify the single biggest uncertainty. Record an error message or exact setting label when there is a problem. Consult the game or platform's legitimate help pages for changes that are specific to an update. Avoid repeating an action that has already failed without learning anything from it. A small verified improvement is more useful than a dramatic, untested workaround.
